classification_reason: A useful scientific field name for IELTS and weather-related content, but a specialized noun with limited broad productive value; the submitted misspelling was normalized to meteorology.

senses.definition: The scientific study of weather and the atmosphere.
senses.example: She studied meteorology before becoming a weather forecaster.
senses.usage_note: Meteorology is the field of study, weather describes short-term atmospheric conditions, and climate describes long-term weather patterns.

synonyms.note: broader and may also include climate and the upper atmosphere

classification_reason: A reusable formal phrase for professional updates and reports when a situation has not changed up to the present but may change later.

senses.definition: Until now; used when something has not happened or is not known, although the situation may change later.
senses.example: No decision has been made as yet.
senses.usage_note: Most common in negative statements and usually placed near the end of the clause.

classification_reason: A useful geometric and technical noun to recognize, but a concrete and domain-dependent item with lower broad productive value.

senses.definition: A three-dimensional shape with two parallel circular ends and one curved surface.
senses.example: The students calculated the volume of the cylinder.
senses.usage_note: A circle is two-dimensional; a cylinder is three-dimensional.

senses.definition: A container, chamber, or machine part shaped approximately like a cylinder.
senses.example: The mechanic found damage inside one of the engine's cylinders.

classification_reason: A broadly reusable adjective for severe treatment, difficult conditions, and unpleasant sensory qualities in conversation, IELTS, and descriptive writing.

senses.example: The proposal received harsh criticism from several experts.

synonyms.note: more formal and does not always imply cruelty

antonyms.note: kind or mild in manner or effect

senses.definition: Difficult or unpleasant because the conditions are extreme.
senses.example: Young plants struggled in the harsh midday sun.

senses.definition: Unpleasantly strong, rough, or irritating to the senses.
senses.example: The harsh lighting made it difficult to concentrate.

classification_reason: A common, productive word for protection from sunlight, color variation, subtle differences, and blocking light or heat.

senses.definition: An area protected from direct sunlight, making it darker and often cooler.
senses.example: We moved our chairs into the shade.
senses.usage_note: This meaning is usually uncountable; common structures include in the shade and provide shade.

synonyms.note: a specific dark shape made when an object blocks light

senses.definition: A particular variation of a color.
senses.example: She chose a darker shade of blue for the office walls.

synonyms.note: refers to the basic color rather than how light or dark it is

senses.definition: A slight difference in meaning, feeling, or quality.
senses.example: The translator preserved the subtle shades of meaning in the original text.
senses.usage_note: Often plural in this abstract sense.

synonyms.note: more formal and especially common for subtle distinctions

senses.definition: To protect someone or something by blocking light or heat.
senses.example: She raised a hand to shade her eyes from the sun.

synonyms.note: broader and can describe protection from many kinds of harm

classification_reason: A common and productive verb for sudden surprise or brief fear in conversation and descriptive writing; the submitted misspelling was normalized to startle.

senses.definition: To cause someone or an animal to feel sudden surprise or brief fear.
senses.example: The sudden alarm startled everyone in the room.
senses.usage_note: Something startles someone; someone can be startled by something or startle at a sudden sound or movement. Startled describes the person or animal, while startling describes the cause.

synonyms.note: does not necessarily suggest a sudden physical reaction
usually suggests stronger or more lasting fear
